items.q: Mei has 24 stickers. Ali gives her 10 more. How many stickers does Mei have now?
items.hint: Gives her more means Mei gets more. Add.

slips.say: 14 is 24 - 10. Ali gives her more, so Mei has more. Add.

tpl.q: Mei has {a} stickers. Ali gives her {b} more. How many stickers does Mei have now?
tpl.hint: Gives her more means Mei gets more. Add.

items.q: A bus has 30 children. 10 children get off. Then 4 children get on. How many children are on the bus now?
items.hint: Two steps. Get off means take away. Get on means add.
steps: Step 1: 10 get off, so take away: 30 - 10 = 20.

slips.say: 44 adds the children who got off. Children who get off leave the bus, so take away.
20 is the answer to Step 1. There is one more step: 4 get on.

tpl.q: A bus has {a} children. {b} children get off. Then {c} children get on. How many children are on the bus now?
tpl.hint: Two steps. Get off means take away. Get on means add.
steps: Step 1: {b} get off, so take away: {a} - {b} = {m}.

items.q: Ben has 15 cards. Ali has 10 more cards than Ben. How many cards does Ali have?
items.hint: Ali has more than Ben, so Ali has the greater number. Add.

slips.say: 5 is 15 - 10. Ali has more than Ben, so add.

tpl.q: Ben has {a} cards. Ali has {b} more cards than Ben. How many cards does Ali have?
tpl.hint: Ali has more than Ben, so Ali has the greater number. Add.

items.q: Siti has 30 beads. She uses 10 beads for a bracelet. Then she buys 6 more. Which number sentence is Step 1?
items.hint: What happens first in the story? Uses means take away.
steps: The first thing that happens is she uses 10 beads.

slips.say: She uses 10 beads, so she has fewer. Take away.
Buying 6 more is Step 2, and it starts from the beads she has left.

items.q: Ali has 24 marbles. Ben has 5 fewer marbles than Ali. How many marbles does Ben have?
items.hint: Ben has fewer, so Ben has the smaller number. Take away.
steps: Ben has fewer, so take away.

slips.say: 29 is 24 + 5. Ben has fewer than Ali, so take away.

tpl.q: Ali has {a} marbles. Ben has {b} fewer marbles than Ali. How many marbles does Ben have?
tpl.hint: Ben has fewer, so Ben has the smaller number. Take away.
steps: Ben has fewer, so take away.

items.q: Mei has 10 beads. Siti has 5 more beads than Mei. How many beads do they have altogether?
items.hint: Two steps. First find how many Siti has. Then put them together.
steps: Step 1: Siti has 5 more than Mei: 10 + 5 = 15.

slips.say: 15 is how many Siti has. Altogether means Mei and Siti together.

tpl.q: Mei has {a} beads. Siti has {b} more beads than Mei. How many beads do they have altogether?
tpl.hint: Two steps. First find how many Siti has. Then put them together.
steps: Step 1: Siti has {b} more than Mei: {a} + {b} = {s}.

items.q: Ravi has 15 marbles. He has 3 more marbles than Mei. How many marbles does Mei have?
items.hint: Ravi has more, so Mei has fewer. Take away.
steps: Ravi has 3 more than Mei, so Mei has 3 fewer than Ravi.

slips.say: 18 is 15 + 3. Ravi has MORE than Mei, so Mei has fewer. Take away.

tpl.q: Ravi has {r} marbles. He has {b} more marbles than Mei. How many marbles does Mei have?
tpl.hint: Ravi has more, so Mei has fewer. Take away.
steps: Ravi has {b} more than Mei, so Mei has {b} fewer than Ravi.

items.q: Mei is in a line. There are 6 children in front of Mei and 4 children behind Mei. How many children are in the line?
items.hint: Draw the line. Did you draw Mei too?
steps: Mei is in the line too: 10 + 1 = 11.

slips.say: 10 leaves out Mei. Count Mei too.

tpl.q: Mei is in a line. There are {f} children in front of Mei and {k} children behind Mei. How many children are in the line?
tpl.hint: Draw the line. Did you draw Mei too?
steps: Mei is in the line too: {s} + 1 = {ans}.

items.q: Ali has 24 cards. He has 6 fewer cards than Ben. How many cards do they have altogether?
items.hint: Ali has fewer, so Ben has more. Find Ben first.

slips.say: 30 is Ben's cards. Altogether means Ali and Ben together.
42 is 24 + 24 - 6. Ali has fewer than Ben, so Ben has more: 24 + 6.

tpl.q: Ali has {a} cards. He has {b} fewer cards than Ben. How many cards do they have altogether?
tpl.hint: Ali has fewer, so Ben has more. Find Ben first.

items.q: Ben has 12 marbles. Mei has 5 more marbles than Ben. Siti has 3 fewer marbles than Mei. How many marbles does Siti have?
items.hint: Find Mei first. Siti is compared with Mei, not with Ben.

slips.say: 9 is 12 - 3. Siti has 3 fewer than Mei, not than Ben.
17 is how many Mei has. Siti has 3 fewer than Mei.

tpl.q: Ben has {a} marbles. Mei has {b} more marbles than Ben. Siti has {c} fewer marbles than Mei. How many marbles does Siti have?

items.q: A shop has 60 pencils. It sells 24 pencils on Monday and 15 pencils on Tuesday. Then a box of 30 pencils comes in. How many pencils does the shop have now?
items.hint: Three things happen, so write three number sentences.

slips.say: 21 is the answer after two steps. A box of 30 pencils comes in, so add.

items.q: Mei, Ali and Ben have 80 shells altogether. Mei has 25 shells. Ali has 10 more shells than Mei. How many shells does Ben have?
items.hint: Find Ali first. Then find how many Mei and Ali have together.

slips.say: 45 is 80 - 35. Ben has the rest after Mei AND Ali.
60 is how many Mei and Ali have together. Ben has the rest.

tpl.q: Mei, Ali and Ben have {T} shells altogether. Mei has {m} shells. Ali has {k} more shells than Mei. How many shells does Ben have?

items.q: There are 15 children in a line, counting Mei. 6 children stand in front of Mei. How many children stand behind Mei?
items.hint: Mei is one of the 15. Take her away too.
steps: 15 children in the line. Mei is one of them.
6 are in front of Mei and 1 is Mei: 6 + 1 = 7.

slips.say: 9 is 15 - 6. Mei is one of the 15 and does not stand behind herself.

tpl.q: There are {n} children in a line, counting Mei. {f} children stand in front of Mei. How many children stand behind Mei?
tpl.hint: Mei is one of the {n}. Take her away too.
steps: {n} children in the line. Mei is one of them.
{f} are in front of Mei and 1 is Mei: {f} + 1 = {u}.

items.q: Make up your own two-step story with one add and one take away. Write the question. Solve it, then check each step.
items.hint: Pick a start number first. Step 1 adds. Step 2 takes away from the new number.
steps: Check Step 1 is one add or one take away.
Check Step 2 starts from the answer to Step 1.
For example: Ali has 20 marbles. He wins 6. Then he loses 4. 20 + 6 = 26, then 26 - 4 = 22.
